item.title: How the migration works
item.description:
A migration is five steps: export the source, move the secrets, sync the structure, cut over, validate. Each step is a circleci-migrate command, and every command that writes is a dry run until you add --apply.

flowchart LR
E[export] --> M[(manifest.json)]
M --> S[secrets transfer]
M --> Y[sync]
S --> Y
Y --> C[cutover]
C --> V[validate]
C -. undo .-> Y

The order of the middle steps changes with the migration type. Follow the runbook for yours: OAuth to GitHub App, OAuth to OAuth or App to App.

The five steps

Step Command What it does
Export export Reads the source org and writes manifest.json and migration-report.md. Read-only.
Secrets secrets transfer Moves secret values from source to destination without writing them to disk. See Secrets.
Sync sync Replays the manifest into the destination org. Dry run unless --apply.
Cutover cutover Pauses source builds and enables destination builds, reversibly. See Cutover.
Validate validate Compares source and destination and exits 1 if anything is missing.

mapping.json tells sync where the destination is. See Mapping.

The manifest

manifest.json is a snapshot of the source org: structure and names, never secret values. It is safe to read, diff and store.

The CircleCI API never returns a secret value, so the manifest lists variable names only. migration-report.md sits next to it. It lists everything captured and the manual follow-ups for your org. Read it before you sync.

Re-export whenever the source changes. Every later command reads the manifest, not the live source.

Dry run first

sync, secrets transfer, cutover and migrate change nothing until you pass --apply. A dry run prints each action as one of these:

Status Meaning
created (would create) --apply will create it.
set (would set) --apply will write the value.
exists Already there; reused. Re-runs are safe.
manual The API cannot do it. The report says what to do by hand.
error A problem. Fix it before you apply.

New projects are created paused: no builds run in the destination until you enable them.

Checks before you start

Run doctor first. It is read-only and checks tokens, org reachability, the allow_api_trigger_with_config setting and the GitHub token.

circleci-migrate doctor --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG"

Check: it exits 0. Exit 1 means a hard failure, such as a missing token or an unreachable org. export, sync and migrate run the same checks on startup; --skip-preflight turns them off.

Tokens and slugs

Use a personal API token for each side, from User Settings > Personal API Tokens. The token's user must be an organization admin of the org it acts on.

Variable Used for
CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN Reading the source org.
CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN Writing the destination org.
CIRCLECI_CLI_TOKEN or CIRCLE_TOKEN Fallback for both sides.
GITHUB_TOKEN Repo read. Needed for OAuth to App and for repos moving to a new GitHub org.

The org slug decides which APIs the tool uses.

Org type Slug Notes
GitHub OAuth gh/<org> Projects are followed to install webhooks.
Bitbucket OAuth bb/<org> Same as GitHub OAuth.
GitHub App, GitLab or standalone circleci/<org-id> Projects use pipeline definitions and triggers. Standalone orgs also carry roles and groups.

Note

One GitHub org can have both an OAuth record (gh/acme) and an App record (circleci/<id>). They are separate orgs. Migrate each one on its own.

For CircleCI Server, pass --host https://circleci.example.com (or set CIRCLECI_CLI_HOST). The default is https://circleci.com.

What sync does

  • Order. Contexts come before projects. A project-type context restriction needs its destination project, so the first run can report it manual. Re-run sync --apply to resolve it.
  • Re-runs. A re-run creates only what is missing and reports the rest exists. A trigger you disabled on purpose is not re-enabled unless you pass --enable-existing-triggers.
  • Enabling builds. After creating projects, sync asks whether to enable builds. --yes answers for you. Do not use --yes while the source is still building, or both orgs build. Use cutover.
  • Danger flags. drop_all_build_requests and require_context_group_restriction are skipped by default because they can freeze a new org. Add --include-danger-flags once the destination is validated.
  • Webhook secrets. CircleCI never returns signing secrets. --webhook-secrets-out webhook-secrets.json writes new ones (mode 0600, never printed). Hand each sender and receiver its new value.
  • Project API tokens. Recreated only with --create-project-tokens, and each one is a new value.
  • Scoping. --skip-org-settings, --skip-contexts, --skip-projects, --skip-pipelines, --skip-extras, --skip-runner, --skip-ciam and --skip-orb leave a section alone.

Orbs and runner classes

Orb namespaces and runner resource classes belong to one org, so they need extra steps.

  • Different destination namespace. sync --dest-orb-namespace republishes every stable version. A notice lists each old/orb to new/orb reference to rewrite in your configs.
  • Same namespace name. An orb namespace cannot exist in two orgs. Ask CircleCI support to move it to the destination org. The orbs move with it and configs need no change.
  • Runner classes. --runner-namespace on export and --dest-runner-namespace on sync recreate class definitions only. Instances and tokens do not move. After a same-name namespace move, classes stay attributed to the source org. Delete the source copies, re-run sync, create new tokens and re-register agents.

The all-in-one command

migrate runs export, sync and validate in one go. With no flags on a terminal it starts a guided walkthrough, then shows a dry run and asks before it applies.

circleci-migrate migrate --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" \
 --transfer-secrets --dest-token-context migration-secrets --include-project-vars

The walkthrough asks which components to migrate (contexts, projects, org settings, extras, orbs, runners) and how to move secrets. Check: it prints a summary with counts and a "Needs attention" list. Add --apply to write.

Use the step-by-step commands for production moves, especially OAuth to GitHub App. migrate cannot do the pause and App-move steps in the right order.

The circleci CLI plugin

circleci run migrate <args> runs circleci-migrate and passes CIRCLE_TOKEN and CIRCLE_URL for you. Bare circleci migrate is not supported.

item.title: Moving secret values
item.description:
Use secrets transfer to move secret values. It sends them from the source org to the destination org without writing them to disk. Use secrets capture only when you need a local, reviewable bundle.

CircleCI never returns a secret value through its API. The only place a value can be read is inside a running pipeline of the org that owns it, so both methods run a short-lived pipeline in your source org.

flowchart LR
CLI[circleci-migrate] -->|inline pipeline| SRC[Source org job]
SRC -->|PUT over TLS| DST[Destination org API]
TOK[(migration-secrets context)] -.->|CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN| SRC

Transfer: the recommended method

The CLI submits one inline pipeline to the source org. Inside it, CircleCI injects the real values and the job writes each one straight to the destination. No value reaches your laptop, an artifact or storage.

The job needs a destination API token. Put it in a context in the source org and pass the context's name. The generated config references ${CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN} and never contains the token.

# 1. In the SOURCE org, create a context named migration-secrets
# holding CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN (a destination org-admin token).

# 2. Dry run: prints the plan, triggers nothing.
circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \
 --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions

# 3. Apply.
circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \
 --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions --enable-trigger --apply

Check: the plan lists each context and project with [create] or [update] and no SKIP lines. After --apply, the destination shows the same variable names.

Note

Anyone who can create pipelines in the source org can read the token context. Use a token with the least access that works, and rotate it when the transfer is done.

Key flags

Flag Use
--dest-org-id Destination org UUID (Organization Settings > Overview). A slug is rejected. --dest-org also works and is resolved for you.
--dest-token-context Name of the source-org context holding the destination token.
--include-project-vars Also move project env vars. Needs the destination project to exist.
--include-ssh-keys Also move additional project SSH keys.
--remove-restrictions Lift project and expression restrictions on contexts for the run, then restore them. Group restrictions are never touched.
--enable-trigger Turn on allow_api_trigger_with_config for the run and restore it afterwards.
--skip-contexts Run only the per-project pipelines, for contexts already moved.
--host-project Source project that runs the context pipeline. Defaults to a suitable one.

Rules that decide the order

  • Destination projects must exist before you move project vars or SSH keys. Contexts are created for you. For a GitHub App destination, create the projects first with sync --apply --skip-pipelines.
  • Projects are matched by name. For a GitHub App destination a source project with no projects entry in mapping.json is matched to the destination project of the same name. An entry always wins. A project that matches neither is shown as SKIP, and the run exits non-zero.
  • The source must still be able to build. Run the transfer before cutover --pause-source. It fails fast and names any paused project.
  • gh/ and bb/ source projects need a way to check out. CircleCI will not start a pipeline on them without a GitHub App pipeline definition or a checkout key. The CLI prefers an App definition and checks this before it changes anything.
  • Move secrets before the GitHub App leaves the source org. After the uninstall the App definitions are gone, and every project then needs a checkout key.

Contexts with project or expression restrictions block the pipeline unless you pass --remove-restrictions. If a restore fails, the CLI prints the exact restriction to re-add.

Capture: the local bundle

secrets capture runs the same kind of pipeline but writes the values to an encrypted artifact, downloads it and saves a local secrets.json. sync --secrets secrets.json then writes the values as it creates each resource.

circleci-migrate secrets capture --manifest manifest.json \
 --encrypt --generate-key --artifact-retention-days 1 --enable-trigger \
 --output secrets.json

Check: secrets.json exists with mode 0600. Capture before sync.

Flag Use
--encrypt On by default. Encrypts the artifact with age so plaintext never sits in CircleCI.
--generate-key Creates a fresh age keypair. Or pass --ssh-public-key and --ssh-private-key.
--artifact-retention-days 1 Shortens how long the artifact stays in CircleCI.
--storage artifact (default), s3 or both. S3 needs --s3-bucket and optionally --s3-prefix.
--context, --project Limit what is captured.
--ssh-keys=false Skip additional SSH keys, which are captured by default.
--remove-restrictions Lift context restrictions for the run. By default restricted contexts are skipped.
--yes Allow an unattended capture of everything. Without it, a non-interactive run with no --context or --project stops.

Restricted contexts skipped at capture can still get their variable names: sync --missing-secrets placeholder creates each name with a placeholder value to fill in later.

secrets decrypt decrypts a bundle you downloaded yourself. For many contexts, the awesomecicd/circleci-org-migration orb runs one extract_context job per context, then a merge job. Use one context per job so same-named variables cannot overwrite each other.

Warning

Do not mix methods for the same resources. A bundle contains plaintext values. Keep it out of git, and delete it after the sync.

After the move

  • Rotate every value that moved. Treat each as exposed once it left the source.
  • Delete the migration-secrets context from the source org, or rotate its token.
  • Delete secrets.json and any decrypted copies, if you used capture.
  • Spot-check the destination: variable names and counts match. Values stay masked, and validate compares names, not values.

What does not move

Item Why What to do
Checkout and deploy key private keys No API returns them. Add a deploy key in the destination. A GitHub App destination needs none.
Webhook signing secrets The source values are unreadable. sync --webhook-secrets-out generates new ones.
Project API token values Shown once, at creation. sync --create-project-tokens mints new values. Repoint consumers.
Restricted-context values The pipeline cannot read them without --remove-restrictions. Re-run with the flag, or fill in by hand.

item.title: The mapping file
item.description:
mapping.json tells the CLI where the destination is. You need it whenever the destination org differs from the source, and the only line that is always required is org.to.

Without it, sync targets the source org named in the manifest and prints a warning. That is correct only when you re-apply into the same org.

When you need it

Situation What to put in mapping.json
Destination org name differs from the source org with from and to.
Slug type changes, such as gh/acme to circleci/<id> org.to set to the destination slug. sync finds or creates App projects by name.
Repos moved to a new GitHub org github_org with from and to, or per-project projects entries.
Same org, same names No mapping file.

migrate also accepts --mapping. For a straight same-name move you can pass --dest-org to migrate instead.

Schema 

{
 "org": { "from": "gh/acme", "to": "circleci/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222" },
 "projects": { "gh/acme/web": "circleci/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/3f1c0b52-7d0e-4a57-9a53-0a6d4f1e9b10" },
 "github_org": { "from": "acme", "to": "acme-new" }
}

All three keys are optional except org.to.

Key Meaning
org Source and destination org slugs. to retargets the destination. from should match the manifest.
projects Source project slug to destination project slug. Optional for most moves.
github_org Rewrites the GitHub owner of every repo. Overrides --dest-github-org. Needs --github-token.

An entry in projects whose key has no / maps a context name to a destination context name. This applies to secrets transfer --mapping.

Project entries are optional

A GitHub App project slug is circleci/<org-id>/<project-id>, and the project ID exists only after the project does. You cannot write these entries up front.

You do not have to. For a source project with no entry, project-type context restrictions and secrets transfer --include-project-vars match the destination project by name. An entry always wins over a name match. Add entries only to review a match or override it.

Generate it

Generate the file from the manifest. For an OAuth destination it fills in every project. For a GitHub App destination, write the org line first, run sync --apply --skip-pipelines to create the projects, then generate.

circleci-migrate mapping generate --manifest manifest.json --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" --output mapping.json

Check: mapping.json has org.from set to your source and org.to set to the destination.

mapping generate writes only org and projects. Add github_org back by hand if you use it.

Partial repo moves

When only some repos changed GitHub org, use projects entries for those repos. Use github_org when every repo moved. Resolving the new repo IDs needs a GitHub token with repo read:

export GITHUB_TOKEN="<github-pat-with-repo-read>"
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --apply

Check: no project shows manual for a wrong external_id.

See also

  • How it works
  • Troubleshooting
  • sync flags

item.title: Cutover
item.description:
cutover switches builds from the source org to the destination, and you can undo it. It pauses the source, then enables the destination, and records every change in a state file so --undo can put it all back.

Without it, you would enable the destination with sync --yes and leave both orgs building. Use cutover whenever the source is still live.

flowchart LR
P[1. pause source] --> M[2. move GitHub App - point of no return]
M --> S[3. sync definitions and triggers]
S --> E[4. enable destination]
P -. undo .-> U[cutover --undo]
E -. undo .-> U

Step 2 applies only to OAuth to GitHub App. After the GitHub App leaves the source org, --undo cannot bring back the source's App triggers.

The flags

cutover is a dry run until you add --apply. Each item prints with its outcome, and the command exits non-zero if any item fails. Re-running is safe.

Flag What it does
--pause-source On each source OAuth project, sets drop-all-build-requests=true (the old value is recorded) and disables the source triggers that are enabled and are not github_oauth triggers. Never unfollows a project.
--pause-org Also sets drop-all-build-requests on the whole source org. Use with --pause-source.
--enable-dest Enables each destination trigger whose source trigger was enabled. A trigger disabled in the source stays disabled.
--undo Restores everything in the state file: source flags, source triggers, and destination triggers it enabled.
--state State file path. Default cutover-state.json, mode 0600.
--manifest, --mapping Needed for pause and enable. With --undo they only check that the state file matches your orgs.

--enable-dest matches triggers by name, then by their fields. An ambiguous match, and a project the manifest shows as paused or not followed, is reported manual and left disabled. Enable that trigger by hand in Project Settings > Triggers. Run sync --apply first so the destination triggers exist.

If a pause fails in the same run, nothing is enabled.

Order for OAuth to GitHub App

The order is fixed. Secrets transfer needs a source that can still build, and the source's App triggers vanish when the App is uninstalled. The full steps are in the runbook.

  1. Freeze merges in the source repos.
  2. sync --skip-pipelines --apply to create the destination projects.
  3. secrets transfer ... --apply while the source can still build.
  4. cutover --pause-source --apply.
  5. Move the GitHub App: uninstall it from the source org, install it from the destination org.
  6. sync --apply --webhook-secrets-out webhook-secrets.json to add definitions and triggers. Answer N at the enable prompt.
  7. cutover --enable-dest --apply.
  8. validate, then a smoke push.

Caution

Step 5 is the point of no return. Uninstalling the GitHub App deletes the source org's App pipelines and triggers. The export is the only record. Pause the source first.

Order for App to App

The destination projects, definitions and triggers already exist after sync --apply, so one step does the switch:

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --enable-dest
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --enable-dest --apply

Check: every item prints set or exists, and the exit code is 0.

Order for OAuth to OAuth

--enable-dest acts on triggers, so it does nothing for an OAuth destination. An OAuth destination goes live when its projects are followed, which is the enable-builds prompt of sync --apply. Once the destination is validated, pause the source:

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --pause-source --apply

Add --pause-org to pause the whole source org.

Undo 

circleci-migrate cutover --undo --apply

Check: the source flags and triggers are back, and the destination triggers it enabled are disabled again.

--undo needs only the state file. It is safe to repeat and fails if the file is missing or belongs to another org. A state record is kept when a change fails in a way that may have applied it (a timeout or a 5xx).

Can undo Cannot undo
Source drop-all-build-requests flags. Moving the GitHub App. A GitHub org connects to one CircleCI org at a time, so uninstall it from the new org and reinstall it on the old one yourself.
Source triggers that cutover disabled, while the App is still installed. Source App triggers, once the App has been uninstalled. Only the flag comes back.
Destination triggers that cutover enabled. Anything you changed outside cutover.

Keep these files safe

  • cutover-state.json: without it --undo has nothing to restore from.
  • webhook-secrets.json: holds the new webhook signing secrets and URLs, mode 0600, never printed. It is merged on re-runs, not overwritten.

Delete both once the cutover is confirmed and every sender and receiver has its new value.

No live source

If nothing is building in the source, skip cutover and enable the destination directly with sync --apply --yes. On a re-run, add --enable-existing-triggers to enable triggers that already exist and are still disabled.

After the cutover

  • Do not build in both orgs. You would pay twice.
  • Repoint what references the old org: service catalogs, badges, Slack and notification integrations, required status checks, and scripts with hard-coded project or context IDs.
  • Rotate the secrets that moved and delete the migration-secrets context.
  • Delete cutover-state.json once you are sure you will not undo.
  • When the destination is healthy, decommission the source: unfollow its projects, archive its contexts, and tell your team and outside contributors.
